title: Topology and compact molecular orbitals in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$
authors: Chenyuan Li, Rwik Dutta, Fang Xie, James R. Chelikowsky, Jennifer Cano, Mit H. Naik, Qimiao Si
abstract: Recent observations of superconductivity in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$ (tWSe$_2$) have motivated theoretical proposals for unconventional pairing mechanisms. A central question is whether band topology plays an essential role in the system's correlation physics. In this letter, we develop a first-principles-based description of the top moiré valence bands in tWSe$_2$. Using density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we identify the bands in the relevant range of twist angles to be topologically non-trivial, with the top valence bands carrying Chern numbers $C=(+1,+1)$ for the $K$ valley. In order to treat the strong correlation physics, we construct compact molecular orbitals directly from the DFT wave functions through a partial Wannierization procedure and with the guidance of spinful $C_{3z}$ symmetry representations. This yields a localized $f$ orbital together with a complementary topological $c$ orbital, allowing us to extract hopping and hybridization amplitudes from first principles. The resulting parameters provide an ab initio benchmark for the effective Hamiltonian. Our work establishes a foundation for understanding superconductivity in moiré TMDs and highlights tWSe$_2$ as a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity.
summary: The paper investigates the electronic structure of twisted bilayer WSe2 to understand its superconducting properties by incorporating band topology. Using DFT and partial Wannierization, the authors confirm the bands are topologically non-trivial and construct an effective Hamiltonian based on two derived molecular orbitals. This provides a crucial theoretical benchmark for studying correlated electron physics in moiré TMDs.
main_problem: The central question is whether band topology plays an essential role in understanding the correlation physics, particularly superconductivity, observed in twisted bilayer WSe2.
main_result: The top moiré valence bands are found to be topologically non-trivial, carrying Chern numbers C=(+1,+1) for the K valley. The authors successfully derived an effective low-energy Hamiltonian using compact molecular orbitals.
method: The study combines first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations with a partial Wannierization procedure guided by symmetry representations to construct localized molecular orbitals.

figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures showing Chern numbers; spatial distributions show orbital localization patterns at high-symmetry points ($\gamma, \kappa$); and plots track hopping parameters and hybridization strength as functions of twist angle.
paper_structure: The work progresses from DFT calculation of moiré bands to identifying their topological nature (Chern numbers). It then employs a partial Wannierization technique guided by symmetry to construct an effective Hamiltonian in terms of two molecular orbitals, allowing for the extraction of key hopping and interaction parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous *ab initio* foundation for modeling strongly correlated systems using topological band theory, which is highly relevant for understanding unconventional superconductivity in 2D materials.
